About the Doctor

Dr. S. Mohammed Thajudeen is a qualified Homoeopathic Physician with a background in Psychology, dedicated to providing individualized, compassionate and patient-centred healthcare.

With academic training in Bachelor of Homoeopathic Medicine and Surgery (BHMS) and a Master's degree in Psychology (MSc Psychology), he brings together an understanding of homoeopathic medical practice and human psychological well-being.

His approach to patient care emphasizes understanding each individual's health concerns, physical symptoms, emotional well-being, lifestyle, personal history and overall health background.

At Dr. Thaj Homoeo Clinic, he believes that effective healthcare begins with listening to patients, understanding their concerns and providing appropriate clinical guidance through individualized assessment and responsible treatment planning.

His practice focuses on holistic patient care, health education, psychological understanding and long-term wellness support.

Professional Philosophy

“Every patient has a unique story. Understanding the individual behind the illness is an important part of providing meaningful healthcare.”
Award & Recognition

COVID-19 Saviour Award

In recognition of his service and contribution during the COVID-19 pandemic, Dr. S. Mohammed Thajudeen was honoured with the COVID-19 Saviour Award. This recognition stands as a meaningful reminder of the dedication, responsibility and compassion that healthcare professionals brought to their communities during an exceptionally challenging time.

The award was presented by Dr. Jesiah Anto Poovendan, Medical Director of Santham Homoeopathy Hospital & Research Centre, in appreciation of service during the pandemic.

Dr. Thajudeen received the honour from Mr. Nakkheeran Gopal (R. Rajagopal), the veteran Tamil journalist widely known as the Founder, Editor and Publisher of the prominent Tamil investigative magazine Nakkheeran.

Recognition: COVID-19 Saviour Award

Psychology-Based Patient Care

My academic background in MSc Psychology provides an additional perspective on understanding human behaviour, emotional responses, thought processes and psychological factors that influence overall well-being.

I believe that healthcare should consider not only the physical symptoms of an individual but also the emotional, behavioural and lifestyle factors that may influence their health.

How Psychology Supports My Clinical Practice

1. Understanding the Mind–Body Connection
Psychological stress, emotional difficulties and lifestyle factors can influence physical well-being. Understanding these interactions helps provide a more comprehensive patient assessment.

2. Patient Communication and Counselling Skills
Effective communication and active listening help patients express their concerns, understand their health conditions and participate more confidently in healthcare decisions.

3. Stress and Emotional Well-being
Understanding psychological stress, anxiety-related symptoms, emotional challenges and their possible impact on daily life.

4. Behavioural and Lifestyle Understanding
Exploring habits, routines, sleep patterns, motivation and behavioural factors that may affect health management.

5. Patient Motivation and Health Awareness
Encouraging patients to develop healthier lifestyle habits, maintain appropriate treatment follow-up and actively participate in their health journey.

Psychological Areas of Interest

  • Stress management and emotional well-being.
  • Anxiety-related concerns.
  • Lifestyle and behavioural patterns.
  • Sleep and relaxation awareness.
  • Emotional support during chronic health conditions.
  • Health behaviour and patient motivation.
  • Mind–body health awareness.

My psychology background complements my medical practice by encouraging a compassionate, empathetic and individual-focused approach to patient care.

Psychological support and health education are provided within the scope of professional qualifications and training. Mental health conditions requiring specialized assessment or treatment are referred to appropriately qualified mental health professionals.
